title: Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky

region.place: Calabar and the Cross River, south-eastern Nigeria
region.label: Efik · Nigeria

setting.period: An Efik story from the Cross River, told for a very long time

sources.author: Elphinstone Dayrell
sources.title: Folk Stories from Southern Nigeria, West Africa (story XVI, “Why the Sun and the Moon live in the Sky”)

provenance.rights: The text is our own retelling of a traditional Efik tale, written for Omramo; it does not use the wording of the cited edition. The cited edition was written down by Elphinstone Dayrell, a colonial district officer, and speaks of “natives”; our retelling drops that voice entirely. The cited edition is in the US public domain (published before 1931); other territories not verified (Dayrell’s death year not verified). Legal review pending (PRD Q23).

culturalReview.reason: Living oral tradition (Efik); the only source is a colonial-era collection. An Efik reader should confirm tone, names and details.

geography.lesson: The Cross River country around Calabar in south-eastern Nigeria, where land, river and sea meet, and where the tide comes up the shore and goes back twice a day.

culture.lesson: Visiting and welcoming guests; a family building a compound of houses round a yard; “why” stories, which the Efik and many other peoples tell to explain the world.

moral.lesson: Think ahead before you make a big promise. The Sun is a kind and generous host, but he promises before he asks how many guests are coming.
moral.reflectionQuestion: What would you have asked the Water before you said yes?

moral: Think ahead before you make a big promise.

card.body: He is a kind friend and a happy host. He says yes first and thinks about it afterwards.

card.label: Character · in Part I and Part II
card.title: The Moon
card.body: She is the Sun’s wife. She builds beside him, wall after wall. When things go wrong, she does not fuss.

portrait.alt: The Moon, a calm woman with a soft silver glow, smiling with a bundle of palm leaves in her arms.

card.label: Character · in Part I and Part II
card.title: The Water
card.body: He is the Sun’s great friend. Fish, crabs and prawns go everywhere with him. He always asks before he comes in.

cultureNote.text: The Efik people live beside this river, in and around the city of Calabar. This story was written down there long ago.

folded.alt: The Sun in a canoe talks with the Water among the mangrove trees.

runs.t: Long ago,
the Sun
runs.name: sun

runs.t: and
the Water
runs.name: water

runs.t: both lived on the earth.
They were great friends.
The Water’s home was down where the
wide river
meets the sea. Mangrove trees stood there on long legs, with their toes in the mud.
Every few days the Sun paddled down in his canoe to visit.

unfolded.alt: Where a wide river meets the sea, the Sun sits in a canoe beside the Water, a friendly face in the waves. Mangroves and palms line the shore.

folded.alt: The Sun in a canoe talks with the Water among the mangrove trees.

runs.t: The two friends talked and laughed all afternoon. The Water’s laugh was deep, like waves rolling in.
But the Water never came to the Sun’s house. Not once.
So one day the Sun asked him.
“My friend, I visit you so often. Why do you never visit me?”

unfolded.alt: Where a wide river meets the sea, the Sun sits in a canoe beside the Water, a friendly face in the waves. Mangroves and palms line the shore.

folded.alt: The Sun in a canoe talks with the Water among the mangrove trees.

runs.t: “Ah,”
said the Water in his deep, slow voice.
“Your house is too small, my friend.”
“I never go anywhere alone. My people come with me, and my people are many. We would push you right out of your own door.”
The Sun laughed. But the Water was not joking.

unfolded.alt: Where a wide river meets the sea, the Sun sits in a canoe beside the Water, a friendly face in the waves. Mangroves and palms line the shore.

folded.alt: The Sun in a canoe talks with the Water among the mangrove trees.

runs.t: “If you want me to come,”
said the Water,
“build a big
compound
. A very big one. Very big indeed!”
“I will!”
said the Sun at once.
“I promise. I will build the biggest compound you ever saw.”
He promised it quickly. He did not stop to ask how many people the Water had.

unfolded.alt: The Sun and the Moon build a great compound: red earth walls, a wide swept yard and a big roof of palm thatch.

folded.alt: The Sun and the Moon tie palm thatch onto the roof of a new house.

runs.t: The Sun hurried home. His wife,
the Moon
runs.name: moon

runs.t: , met him at the door with a wide, bright smile.
“The Water is coming to visit!”
he said.
“We must build a compound big enough for all his people.”
“How many people?”
asked the Moon.
“Many,”
said the Sun.
“I forgot to ask.”

unfolded.alt: The Sun and the Moon build a great compound: red earth walls, a wide swept yard and a big roof of palm thatch.

folded.alt: The Sun and the Moon tie palm thatch onto the roof of a new house.

runs.t: “Then we had better build it very big,”
said the Moon calmly.
So they began the very next morning. They pressed red earth into thick walls. They swept a yard as wide as a field.
They tied palm leaves into thatch for a great roof.

unfolded.alt: The Sun and the Moon build a great compound: red earth walls, a wide swept yard and a big roof of palm thatch.

folded.alt: The Sun and the Moon tie palm thatch onto the roof of a new house.

runs.t: Day after day they built. Wall after wall, room after room, roof after roof.
At last it was done. It was bigger than the market. It was the biggest compound anyone had ever seen.
“There,”
said the Sun, wiping his hands.
“Room for everybody.”
The Moon looked at the great empty yard.
“We shall see,”
she said.

unfolded.alt: On a bright day the Water flows in at the gate of the compound with fish and crabs, while the Sun and the Moon climb up onto the thatched roof.

folded.alt: The Sun and the Moon sit on the roof as water full of fish fills the yard.

runs.t: The next morning, a deep voice called at the gate.
“Is it safe for me to come in?”
“Yes, come in, my friend!”
called the Sun.
Whoosh!
In flowed the Water, cool and shining, across the yard. With him came little silver fish and crabs that walked sideways.

unfolded.alt: On a bright day the Water flows in at the gate of the compound with fish and crabs, while the Sun and the Moon climb up onto the thatched roof.

folded.alt: The Sun and the Moon sit on the roof as water full of fish fills the yard.

runs.t: More water came, and more. Soon it was as deep as the Sun’s knees.
Fish swam in at the door. A crab sat down on the Moon’s best stool.
“Is it still safe for me to come in?”
asked the Water.
“Yes, yes, come in, my friend!”
said the Sun. He had promised, after all.

unfolded.alt: On a bright day the Water flows in at the gate of the compound with fish and crabs, while the Sun and the Moon climb up onto the thatched roof.

folded.alt: The Sun and the Moon sit on the roof as water full of fish fills the yard.

runs.t: In came bigger fish, and prawns with long whiskers, and more crabs than anyone could count.
The water rose as high as a tall man’s head.
The Sun and the Moon scrambled up onto the roof.
“My friend,”
rumbled the Water,
“do you still want my people to come in?”

unfolded.alt: On a bright day the Water flows in at the gate of the compound with fish and crabs, while the Sun and the Moon climb up onto the thatched roof.

folded.alt: The Sun and the Moon sit on the roof as water full of fish fills the yard.

runs.t: The Sun looked at the Moon. The Moon looked at the Sun.
It is hard to send away a guest you begged to come.
“Yes,”
said the Sun, more quietly.
“Come in, my friend.”
So in came the rest of the Water’s people. Up went the water, over the walls, over the thatch, over the top of the roof.

unfolded.alt: The Sun and the Moon sit high in a pale sky. Far below, calm wide water covers everything but the tip of a thatched roof and the tops of the palms.

folded.alt: The Sun and the Moon side by side in a pale sky above calm water.

runs.t: There was nowhere left to stand. So the Sun took the Moon’s hand, and up they went.
Up past the palm tops. Up past the birds. Up, up,
up
into the sky.
Far below, the Water spread out wide and calm. Only the tip of the roof showed.
“Well,”
said the Moon,
“there is plenty of room up here.”

unfolded.alt: The Sun and the Moon sit high in a pale sky. Far below, calm wide water covers everything but the tip of a thatched roof and the tops of the palms.

folded.alt: The Sun and the Moon side by side in a pale sky above calm water.

runs.t: And there they have lived ever since. The Sun shines from the sky by day. The Moon smiles down by night.
The Water still misses his friends. Twice a day he
creeps up the shore
to see if they have come home.
Then, very politely, he goes away again.
